primary_source_audit.supports: Chameleon Team, “Chameleon: Mixed-Modal Early-Fusion Foundation Models,” v1 (2024) . PDF pp. 4–8: discrete tokenizer, interleaved training, stability, and resource context. The tokenizer’s OCR limitation is specific to that model.

primary_source_audit.reading_status: Selected relevant original PDF pages; no full-paper certificate
primary_source_audit.supports: Razavi, van den Oord, and Vinyals, “Generating Diverse High-Fidelity Images with VQ-VAE-2,” v1 (2019) . PDF p. 2: lossy nearest-codebook-vector representation. The binary-label collision is an original counterexample.

primary_source_audit.reading_status: Selected relevant original PDF pages; no full-paper certificate
primary_source_audit.supports: Zhou et al., “Transfusion: Predict the Next Token and Diffuse Images with One Multi-Modal Model,” v1 (2024) . PDF pp. 4–9: diffusion loss, continuous latent representations, hybrid mask, decoding, and controlled-comparison methods. Avoiding quantization does not remove VAE compression loss.

primary_source_audit.reading_status: Selected relevant original PDF pages; no full-paper certificate
primary_source_audit.supports: Liang et al., “Mixture-of-Transformers: A Sparse and Scalable Architecture for Multi-Modal Foundation Models,” v2 (2025) . PDF pp. 6–13, 15–16, 19–21, 25, 28, 31–32: global attention with modality-specific weights, comparator confounds, task-specific experiments, sparse combinations, and hardware-bound timing scope.

primary_source_audit.reading_status: Selected relevant original PDF pages; no full-paper certificate
primary_source_audit.supports: Shi et al., “LMFusion: Adapting Pretrained Language Models for Multimodal Generation,” v4 (2025) . PDF pp. 4–7: frozen text components, joint attention, adaptation data/cost boundary, and metrics. The earlier v1 was titled LlamaFusion.

primary_source_audit.reading_status: Selected relevant original PDF pages; no full-paper certificate
primary_source_audit.supports: Deng et al., “Emerging Properties in Unified Multimodal Pretraining,” v1 (2025) . PDF pp. 3–6, 10–13, 19: BAGEL branches, visual encoders, clean/noisy masking, objective balancing, and IntelligentBench’s CoT comparison. Automated-judge results are not a physical-reasoning certificate.
